newsitem.title: USA: Goldman Sachs Q1 pre-tax profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs Q1 pre-tax profits rise.

text.p: Goldman Sachs & Co saw its fiscal first quarter pre-tax earnings rise to $905 million from $565 million in the comparable period a year ago, the company's chief financial officer said.

In a statement outlining results for the quarter, Goldman Chief Financial Officer John Thain said the privately-held investment bank's revenues rose to $1.96 billion from $1.46 billion a year ago. Expenses rose to $1.05 billion from $899 million, reflecting added staffing.

The company's headcount stands at about 9,000, up about 10 percent versus a year ago. Capital at the firm is now about $5.4 billion, up from about $5.25 billion at the end of the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996.
"We have benefitted from strong financial markets," Thain said, "and will continue to invest in and build our professional and business capabilities."
Goldman Sachs' fiscal first quarter ended February 28.
